research_scope: Four manually reviewed phrase-specific aliases into three disjoint missing construction identities: final quotient topology, ordinary comma category and over/slice category.

aliases.reason: These usages share the final topology induced on the exact surjective target by q:X→Q. For strict maps the target is the image f(X), not the entire ambient Y; for coequalizers the target is a quotient set. Both instantiate the same final-topology construction, without identifying quotient topology with a quotient set or subspace topology. Reviewed raw phrase 'quotient topology induced by surjection X→f(X)' against canonical 'quotient topology on Y for f' in their full source formulation contexts. Source phrasing and occurrence identities remain immutable.

The same ordinary comma category construction specializes by fixing an object j on the left or right, yielding j↓H versus H↓j. They have opposite arrow orientations in each source, which must remain visible, but neither demands an invertible connecting arrow. The separate iso-comma category is not substituted. Reviewed raw phrase 'comma category (H↓j)' against canonical 'comma category (j↓H)' in their full source formulation contexts. Source phrasing and occurrence identities remain immutable.

Both occurrences refer to the overcategory C/U whose objects are arrows V→U and morphisms triangles over U. Changing the bound base object name from U to X does not change the general slice-category meaning. This remains a specific construction, not a synonym for unrestricted comma or iso-comma categories. Reviewed raw phrase 'slice category C/X' against canonical 'slice category C/U' in their full source formulation contexts. Source phrasing and occurrence identities remain immutable.
